references.text: Expands on the command to consecrate all firstborn to the Lord, both of humans and animals, as a reminder of the exodus from Egypt.
Repeats the command to give the firstborn son to the Lord.
Confirms that all firstborn belong to the Lord, including the redemption of firstborn sons.
The Lord declares that all firstborn belong to him from the day he struck down the firstborn in Egypt.
Confirms that all firstborn in Israel belong to the Lord, both of humans and animals.
Laws concerning the redemption of firstborn humans and unclean animals.
Every male firstborn of cattle and sheep shall be consecrated to the Lord.
The firstborn of animals already belongs to the Lord and cannot be dedicated as a special offering.
Jesus was presented in the temple as the firstborn son, in accordance with Moses' law to consecrate the firstborn to the Lord.
Refers to the assembly of the firstborn who are enrolled in heaven.
Confirmation that the birthright has been transferred to the Levites as a substitute for the Egyptian firstborn.
Explains how the requirement for firstborns in Exodus is fulfilled through substitution with the Levites.
Specific instruction on the substitution of firstborns with the Levites, fulfilling the requirement in Exodus.
Expands the principle from Exodus by specifying that human firstborns must be redeemed.
Direct confirmation and specification of the law of the firstborn given in Exodus 13.
